frequency_question: How often do such bills successfully pass the U.S. Senate with exact textual matches to citizenship-verification requirements within the allotted timeframe?
membership_rule: Members are major partisan voting or election administration reform bills requiring specific federal mandates (like voter ID or proof of citizenship) voted on in the Senate since 1994. Excluded are broad bipartisan compromises and non-electoral omnibus bills.

cases.name: National Voter Registration Act amendments / various voter ID amendments
SAVE Act (House versions/Senate companion attempts prior to window end)

provenance_note: 2 cases named, 5 claimed via skeleton x multiplier (2.5x); rate of 0% from only 5 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 5 major distinct legislative pushes or vehicle amendments for strict federal proof-of-citizenship/voter ID mandates in the Senate since 1994; all missed passage of the exact standalone criteria.
known_gaps: Minor committee-level voice votes or riders that lacked strict standalone tracking are excluded.
skeleton: Major partisan voter eligibility bills introduced in the Senate since 1994 grouped by legislative attempts; almost all fail cloture or exact text matching due to Senate filibuster rules and narrow majorities.
multiplier: 0 hits out of estimated 5 major attempts at strict standalone federal voter eligibility/ID mandates passing the Senate cleanly.
validity_reason: Remains valid as long as current Senate filibuster thresholds and polarized partisan dynamics on election administration persist.
